divergences.next: A continuous price monitor between runs is on the backlog (P2).
divergences.text: The paper simulator cannot hold stop orders. Every open position carries a stop and target in the journal, and each scheduled run checks the price against them and sells what has breached. Between runs a stop is not watched, so a fast move can go further than the stop before the next run acts.
divergences.title: Stops are watched by the desk, not held at the broker

divergences.text: The rules forbid shorting (margin cost and forced-liquidation risk). A bearish view is expressed with a long put, where the most that can be lost is the premium paid.
divergences.title: No short selling

divergences.next: Let the desk push to the repo, then add the publish script as the last step of every run.
divergences.text: The desk writes its journal to a private drive. A publish script copies a safe, redacted version of the numbers to this site, and today a person has to run it. Refresh can only check whether a newer publish exists.

planned.name: Option spread (two legs)

readiness.label: Platform limit
readiness.needs: A change to the desk's order rules to allow a sold option leg, with a written decision first.
readiness.reason: The desk can only send one-leg orders: buy one call or buy one put. A spread needs two legs, one of them sold, and the desk's safety checks and the moomoo order link do not allow a sold option. The challenge rules also recommend single-leg options.

planned.what: Buys one option and sells another on the same stock at the same time, so the most it can lose is fixed up front.

readiness.reason: The one-page plan is written, but the desk has no code for it yet and no share of the account has been set aside. The plan proposes 15%.

planned.what: Once a week, ranks 12 sector funds by how strongly they have been rising and holds the top three, for example chips or software when AI stocks are hot. Sells a fund when it drops out of the top five or falls under its 50-day average.

strategies.name: Regime rotation (ETFs)
strategies.what: Holds a basket of broad ETFs. Each run it reads the market gate (risk on, neutral or risk off), leans into the strongest sleeves and moves to cash when the gate turns risk off.

strategies.cap_note: Shares bought by the tactical lane, all names together.
strategies.name: Tactical stocks (desk picks)
strategies.what: The desk picks single stocks from a short approved list (MSFT plus the five defensives KO, PG, JNJ, PEP and MCD). Every trade needs its own written reason, a stop and a target worth at least 1.5 times the risk.

strategies.cap_note: Option premium at risk, all contracts together.
strategies.name: Tactical options (single leg)
strategies.what: The same desk picks, but bought as one call (expecting a rise) or one put (expecting a fall) instead of shares. The most it can lose is what was paid. Test runs to Fri 27 Nov.

strategies.cap_note: Up to 4 trades of 5% each, closed the same day. Not part of the sum rule.
strategies.name: Intraday breakout (scalp)
strategies.what: Watches five chip stocks on one-minute bars and buys when the price breaks above the last five bars. Stop at 0.25%, target at twice the risk, out within 20 minutes and always flat before the close.
